text: I persuaded Bai Ganya to walk to the opera and get tickets for the evening. They were performing the ballet "Ruppenfeh" and I don't remember what else. We passed the Greek cafe, turned into the "Mendl" cafe, where the Bulgarians gather, and headed for the "St. Stephen" church. Here in the square I invited Bai Ganya to stop by a pastry shop, as I had no idea that the character of Don Juan could get under Bai Ganya's skin. But civilization works wonders! I must tell you that I was studying in Vienna at the time; I had gone there during the holidays and was just returning, so on the way to Vienna we met Bai Ganya. I went to this pastry shop often and got to know the cashier very well, a pretty and cheerful girl, cheerful, but she behaved well and did not allow liberties. And imagine, gentlemen, we enter the pastry shop with Uncle Ganya, we approach the buffet, the girl greets me cheerfully with a welcome, I answer her with some playful pleasantries and go back to choose something sweet, and at that moment an indignant scream deafens the entire establishment...
“What happened, Uncle Ganyo, did you do something to her?” I shouted anxiously and angrily.
"I didn't, brother, what have I done?" replied Uncle Ganyo in a shaky voice.

The girl, extremely angry, her face red, told me in a loud voice that Uncle Ganyo had insulted her with an act, grabbed her and not only grabbed her, but also twisted his arm with clenched teeth. She wanted to call the police. Scandal!

"Get out of here soon, Uncle Ganya; if the police catch you, your job is done for, go upstairs, I'll catch up with you," I shouted with feigned indignation and almost burst out laughing, looking at Uncle Ganya's tragicomic figure.
– What's wrong with me! – said Bai Ganyo with courage on the way out. – Is Sankim honest? I know the women here. Show me the purse – suddenly I'm hungry, but it's not simple, Bai Ganyo!...

I was destined to end my impressions of that day with another adventure, the hero of which was our Mr. Gagnot again. As I told you, the ballet "Ruppenfee" was being performed at the opera. We took seats in the ground floor. The theater was full. Mr. Gagnot's dark clothes were striking in contrast to the general dark background of the costumes. The curtain rose. Silence - dead. Everyone's eyes were fixed on the fantastically decorated stage. I felt that Mr. Gagnot was stirring something, groaning, to my right, but I could not take my eyes off the stage: the ballet scenes were constantly changing according to the movement of a magic wand, various groups of ballerinas appeared, disappeared; on the stage there was now darkness, now monochromatic, now multi-colored light - a fairy tale! One of the ballerinas separated from the general group, took small, quick steps towards the proscenium, stopped, jumped and floated through the air, supported only by the tip of one leg... At that very moment, behind me, a hysterical ha-ha-ha-ha! split the air. I turn to the left - all the rows behind me are giggling and pointing to something on my right. Something bad instantly crossed my mind. I turn to Bai Ganya... God! What do I see! Bai Ganya took off his sleeves and unbuttoned his vest, which was tightening him from the muskets stuffed into his belt: one of the theater employees grabbed his sleeve with two fingers and made completely unambiguous signs with his head for him to come out; Bai Ganya turned to face him and also answered him with signs - "Sankim, who are you going to scare?" This very Babaite moment elicited hysterical laughter from a little girl sitting behind us, and this laughter infected the entire theater. A picture! And imagine, gentlemen, I look, overcome with shame, towards the boxes – as if someone was pulling me to look – and my eyes meet the eyes of an entire familiar German family, in which I was very well received, and in their eyes I read sincere pity for my desperate situation. And at that time, Uncle Ganyo was pulling me energetically by the sleeve:
– Come on, let's go out, leave these Jews alone – they'll fall into my hands, wait!...
